name: cx-sequence~p1
task: First find the key and pick it up. Then open the locked door, enter the room, and pick up the ball.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the task commands the first step ('First find the key and pick it up'), so key_found and has_matching_key are commanded steps. With the hard Precedence chain key_found → has_matching_key → ... and the hard Existence(target_picked_up), the chain forces key_found, but has_matching_key is only the middle of the chain and its hard Existence(has_matching_key) likewise repeats what the chain forces — but the real issue is Existence(key_found): it repeats what Precedence(key_found, has_matching_key) plus Existence(has_matching_key) already force. In a stated order the hard Existence of the last step and the hard Precedence chain force every earlier step; the intermediate Existence(key_found) and Existence(has_matching_key), Existence(target_door_open), Existence(target_room_entered) only repeat what the chain plus Existence(target_picked_up) already force. Remove those redundant Existence clauses (key_found, has_matching_key, target_door_open, target_room_entered) and keep Existence(target_picked_up) with the four hard Precedence clauses.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) requires the ball; the Precedence chain (key_found→has_matching_key→target_door_open→target_room_entered→target_picked_up) captures the stated order, and the hard chain forces the earlier steps, so no extra Existence clauses are needed.
